prerequisites: To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all first-year courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the functioning of the main automobile and railway systems.
Ability to perform vehicle dynamics calculations.
Ability to design automobile and railway systems and components.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the theory of automobiles. The automobile vehicle, concept. Main requirements of the automobile vehicle. The human-machine-environment system. Objectives and scope of automobile vehicle theory.

Interaction between the vehicle and the road surface. General and mechanical characteristics of the tire, mechanical characteristics. Study of longitudinal (traction, braking) and transverse (drift) forces. Soil-wheel mathematical models.
Aerodynamics of automobiles. Aerodynamic actions on solids, general concepts. Aerodynamic actions on the automobile vehicle.

Longitudinal dynamics. Performance. Longitudinal dynamics: Resistance to movement and fundamental equation of longitudinal movement. Performance: estimation of vehicle performance. Maximum tractive effort and adherence limitation.
Braking of automobiles. Forces and moments acting in the braking process. Conditions imposed by adherence for optimal braking. Braking system and braking process. The ABS system.
The transmission system. Engine and transmission characteristics. Principles of design of the transmission system and its elements.

Vehicle lateral dynamics. Analysis of vehicle transverse behavior. Steering system. Steering geometry. Low-speed maneuverability. Skid and rollover limit speed. Vehicle directional behavior in steady state.

The suspension system. Analysis of vehicle vertical behavior and the suspension system. Vibrations on the vehicle, action on humans. The suspension system: mathematical model. Suspension kinematics. Suspension systems: elastic and absorption elements. Influence of suspension on vehicle behavior. Suspension settings.

Safety systems in automobiles. Active and passive safety. Driving assistance systems: traction and stability control, ABS. Influence of driving technique. Passive safety: deformable structures, safety cell, seat belts, airbag. Analysis of road infrastructure: Influence of road infrastructure on vehicle dynamic behavior. Major reforms in automobiles: Regulations and execution of reforms.
Railways. Railway infrastructures. Typology of railway vehicles. Railway vehicle systems: traction, suspension, etc. Rolling elements.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practice attendance and report/asynchronous questionnaires

assessment_rules: The course is passed if a final grade of five or more is obtained. In the first edition, a theoretical-practical exam contributes 40% (min 1.5/4), lab practice activities and reports 30% (min 1/3), and asynchronous questionnaires/optional assignments 30% (min 1/3). If the minimum in the theoretical-practical exam is not reached, the final grade is the exam score out of 10. The lab grade is conserved for the second edition, while the problem-solving grade is not. In the second edition, the exam contributes 70% (min 2.75/7). For students with official global evaluation, a lab practices exam contributes 30% (min 1/3), and a theoretical-practical exam 70% (min 2.75/7). Unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized electronic devices) will result in a global failing grade of 0.0 for the current academic year.
